precepts.text: A man cut off from his heritage was discontinued from the inheritance the Most High gave him, which is why the name has to be found written in this book of records to have a part.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

precepts.why:
The Levites and the priests “were recorded chief of the fathers”, and “The sons of Levi, the chief of the fathers, were written in the book of the chronicles”. This is the book of records, our ancestors written down.

Why does the name have to be found written in this book? Because of what Jeremiah said would happen to Judah: “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

A man cut off from his heritage was discontinued from the inheritance the Most High gave him, made to serve his enemies in a land he did not know. To have a part in that heritage again, the name has to be found written in the record, as the chief of the Levites and their brethren were written, giving thanks according to the commandment of David the man of God, ward over against ward.

points: These are the priests and Levites that went up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, and the rest named as the chiefs of the priests and their brethren in the days of Jeshua.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: The Levites are named, Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, and Mattaniah who was over the thanksgiving, with Bakbukiah and Unni set over against them in the watches. This is the register of those who returned to serve.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: The priestly succession is traced: Jeshua begat Joiakim, Joiakim begat Eliashib, and the line continues through Joiada, Jonathan, and Jaddua.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: In the days of Joiakim the chief of the fathers of each priestly house are named. This is the record kept so the priesthood could be proven by descent, generation after generation.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: The Levites and priests were recorded as chief of the fathers down to the reign of Darius the Persian, and the sons of Levi were written in the book of the chronicles until the days of Johanan.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: The chief of the Levites, Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua, gave thanks according to the commandment of David, ward over against ward. This is the book of the chronicles, our ancestors written down in the record.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites out of all their places to bring them into Jerusalem to keep the dedication with gladness, with thanksgivings, singing, cymbals, psalteries, and harps.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: The sons of the singers gathered from the plain country round about Jerusalem and from the villages they had built for themselves. The priests and Levites purified themselves, then purified the people, the gates, and the wall.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: Nehemiah brought up the princes of Judah upon the wall and appointed two great companies that gave thanks, one going to the right hand upon the wall toward the dung gate, the other going the opposite way.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: The companies are named, priests with trumpets and Levites with the musical instruments of David the man of God, Ezra the scribe going before one and Nehemiah with the other, until the two companies stood in the house of God.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: That day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced, for the Most High had made them rejoice with great joy; the wives and children rejoiced also, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar off.

note.label: Nehemiah 12: The Priests, the Levites, and the Dedication of the Wall

points: Men were appointed over the chambers for the treasures, the offerings, the firstfruits, and the tithes, and both singers and porters kept the ward of their God according to the commandment of David and of Solomon his son, and the portions were given every day.
